correctness.rationale: For a nonempty reverse-complement-closed 5-mer code, the first-letter set P is disjoint from its Watson--Crick complement. A complement-preserving letter permutation moves P into {A,C}; all words then lie in {A,C}Σ^3{G,T} (256 candidates). Its odd-length reverse-complement orbits all have size two. Independence from all proper cross-prefix/suffix overlaps leaves 56 admissible orbits and a simple incompatibility graph with 412 edges. The 18 listed cliques partition all 56 orbit vertices, so an independent set has at most 18 pairs, i.e. 36 codewords. The listed 18 orbit indices form an independent set, proving the bound attainable. This is a complete finite certificate, not an unverified solver bound. Independently reimplemented DNA reverse complement, raw orbits, admissibility, all ordered overlap conflicts, graph, partition and 18-pair witness in JavaScript: 128 raw orbits, 56 admissible, 412 conflicts, 18 genuine disjoint cliques, zero missing edges, 18 pairwise compatible witness orbits and no errors. Both Python verifier implementations were inspected from the assigned tree. The exact finite count proves the fixed-length theorem; it claims nothing for longer lengths.
